topic: Britain's land on Cyprus and five more strange borders, ending on India's enclave swap
hook: Your British holiday could be on Cyprus, and the map says that land still belongs to the UK.
title: Britain Owns Land in Cyprus (+5 More Strange Borders)
description: Britain still owns two pieces of Cyprus, an island in the European Union. This countdown of six strange borders starts with a road that stops for planes and ends with the India-Bangladesh enclaves, where one field sat inside land inside land inside land. Every place is real and you can find each one on a map.

chapters.title: 6. The road that stops for planes
3. The village joined by one point

scenes.narration: Your British holiday could be on Cyprus, and the map says that land still belongs to the UK.
scenes.headline: Britain In Cyprus

scenes.narration: Britain owns two pieces of an island that is itself part of the European Union.
scenes.headline: UK Land, EU Island

scenes.narration: That is only number two on today's list of borders that make no sense.
scenes.headline: Borders That Make No Sense

scenes.narration: Number one is in India, where one tiny patch of land sat inside three other patches of land.
scenes.headline: India's Strangest

scenes.narration: Six borders, each stranger than the last. Stay to the end and you will see how a map can tie itself in knots.
scenes.headline: Each One Stranger

scenes.narration: And the fun part is that every one of these is real, with a place you can find on a map.
scenes.headline: All Of It Is Real

scenes.narration: Here is how it works: I count down from six, and the strangest border comes last.
scenes.headline: Countdown From Six

scenes.narration: We start with a road where cars have to stop for aeroplanes.
scenes.headline: Cars Stop For Planes

scenes.narration: Number six: a road that closes whenever a plane lands.
scenes.headline: Number Six

scenes.narration: Gibraltar is a small British territory at the southern tip of Spain, joined to Spanish land by one border.
scenes.headline: Gibraltar

scenes.narration: Right beside that border, the airport runway cuts straight across the main road.
scenes.headline: Runway Across A Road

scenes.narration: The road is called Winston Churchill Avenue, and it carries everyday traffic like any other town road.
scenes.headline: Winston Churchill Avenue

scenes.narration: When a plane is about to land or take off, barriers come down and everybody has to wait.
scenes.headline: Barriers Come Down

scenes.narration: Cars, scooters and people on foot all stop while the aircraft rolls across the road in front of them.
scenes.headline: Everyone Waits

scenes.narration: Then the barriers lift and the traffic carries on, as if nothing happened.
scenes.headline: Then Life Carries On

scenes.narration: So if you walk in from Spain, you may cross a runway before you even reach the shops.
scenes.headline: Walk Over A Runway

scenes.narration: The airport sits squeezed between the sea and the rock, so there was little room to build around the road.
scenes.headline: No Room To Spare

scenes.narration: It is one of the very few places in the world where a main road crosses an active runway.
scenes.headline: A Very Rare Crossing

scenes.narration: The rock behind it is tiny, yet Britain has held it for more than three hundred years.
scenes.headline: Tiny Rock, Big Claim

scenes.narration: Spain still claims it, so this small border is never just a road.
scenes.headline: Spain Still Claims It

scenes.narration: But the next place has a bigger problem: you cannot drive to it from its own country.
scenes.headline: Next: Cut Off

scenes.narration: Number five: an American town you can only reach by driving through Canada.
scenes.headline: Number Five

scenes.narration: Point Roberts is part of Washington state, yet it hangs off the bottom of a Canadian peninsula.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: The border follows a straight line on the map, the forty-ninth parallel, and the town ended up on the wrong side of it.
scenes.headline: A Straight Line

scenes.narration: The Canadian part of that peninsula is a normal suburb, and Point Roberts is just the American tip at the end.
scenes.headline: The American Tip

scenes.narration: So if you live there and want to drive to the rest of America, you must go through Canada first.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Canada

scenes.narration: That means two border checks just to drive home inside your own country.
scenes.headline: Two Border Checks

scenes.narration: Minnesota has a similar place called the Northwest Angle, reachable by land only through Canada.
scenes.headline: Northwest Angle

scenes.narration: Both exist because old treaties were drawn with straight lines on old maps, and nobody checked the real land.
scenes.headline: Old Maps, Real People

scenes.narration: On a map these pieces look like mistakes. In real life, people go to school and buy groceries there.
scenes.headline: People Live Here

scenes.narration: Their shops, post and school buses all depend on crossing a border that most of us never think about.
scenes.headline: Daily Life, Two Countries

scenes.narration: The next town does something even odder with money.
scenes.headline: Next: Two Currencies

scenes.narration: Number four: a German town completely surrounded by Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Number Four

scenes.narration: Büsingen sits on the Rhine, and every road out of it leads into Swiss land.
scenes.headline: Büsingen

scenes.narration: It has been part of Germany for centuries, even though Switzerland surrounds it on all sides.
scenes.headline: German, Surrounded

scenes.narration: It is German, yet its shops and people also use Swiss francs in daily life.
scenes.headline: Euros And Francs

scenes.narration: Its cars carry special number plates with the letters BÜS, so everyone knows where they come from.
scenes.headline: BÜS Number Plates

scenes.narration: A German town, Swiss money, and a border that does not follow any hill or river.
scenes.headline: A Border Of Its Own

scenes.narration: It dates back to old territorial deals, and it stayed because nobody ever wanted to change it.
scenes.headline: Left Over From History

scenes.narration: So the map shows a small dot of Germany floating inside Swiss land.
scenes.headline: Germany Inside Switzerland

scenes.narration: If you enjoy strange places like this, this is a good moment to subscribe, because tomorrow brings more of them.
scenes.headline: Subscribe For More

scenes.narration: It is also a nice reminder that a country border is a human decision, not a natural one.
scenes.headline: Borders Are Human Choices

scenes.narration: Now a village that connects to its own country at one single point.
scenes.headline: Next: A Single Point

scenes.narration: Number three: an Austrian village that touches the rest of Austria at a single point.
scenes.headline: Number Three

scenes.narration: Jungholz sits high in the Alps, and Germany lies around it on almost every side.
scenes.headline: Jungholz

scenes.narration: Its border with the rest of Austria is not a line at all. It is one point on a mountain.
scenes.headline: One Point

scenes.narration: In everyday life, that means villagers drive through Germany to reach most places in Austria.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Germany

scenes.narration: Imagine telling a friend you live in Austria, then driving through Germany to get home.
scenes.headline: Austria Via Germany

scenes.narration: A single dot on a map is all that keeps the village legally Austrian.
scenes.headline: A Dot Keeps It Austrian

scenes.narration: It also shows that a border can be one point, one line, or an entire river.
scenes.headline: Point, Line Or River

scenes.narration: Austria and Germany get along perfectly, so nobody minds. But few borders are held together this thinly.
scenes.headline: Held By A Thread

scenes.narration: Next, the one from the start: British land on an EU island.
scenes.headline: Next: Cyprus

scenes.narration: Number two: land on Cyprus that belongs to the United Kingdom.
scenes.headline: Number Two

scenes.narration: Cyprus became independent from Britain in 1960, but Britain kept two areas for its military.
scenes.headline: Independent In 1960

scenes.narration: They are called Akrotiri and Dhekelia, and together they are the British Sovereign Base Areas.
scenes.headline: Akrotiri And Dhekelia

scenes.narration: Sovereign means they are not rented. Legally, that land is British territory.
scenes.headline: British Territory

scenes.narration: Together they cover less than three percent of the island, but they appear as British land on the map.
scenes.headline: Less Than 3 Percent

scenes.narration: Britain also kept them because of their position, close to the Middle East and the eastern Mediterranean.
scenes.headline: A Useful Location

scenes.narration: RAF Akrotiri is a working air base on the southern coast of the island.
scenes.headline: RAF Akrotiri

scenes.narration: Cyprus joined the European Union in 2004, so the EU has an island with Britain still sitting on it.
scenes.headline: EU Island, UK Land

scenes.narration: Cypriot villages and farms sit inside these areas, and people live ordinary lives there.
scenes.headline: Villages Inside

scenes.narration: The areas are run by a military administrator rather than a normal government.
scenes.headline: Run By The Military

scenes.narration: And the island has another border: a line that has split it in two since 1974.
scenes.headline: The Island Is Split

scenes.narration: That line cuts through the capital, Nicosia, so one city has people on both sides of a closed street.
scenes.headline: A Divided Capital

scenes.narration: So a single island carries a British border, a European border, and a divided capital.
scenes.headline: Three Borders, One Island

scenes.narration: And yet number one is still stranger, and it is right here in India.
scenes.headline: Next: India

scenes.narration: Number one: a border so tangled that India and Bangladesh had to swap whole villages.
scenes.headline: Number One

scenes.narration: In West Bengal, near the old kingdom of Cooch Behar, little islands of one country sat inside the other.
scenes.headline: Cooch Behar

scenes.narration: Cooch Behar was once a princely state, and it joined India in 1949, two years after independence.
scenes.headline: Joined India In 1949

scenes.narration: These pockets are called enclaves, and for decades there were over a hundred and fifty of them.
scenes.headline: Enclaves Everywhere

scenes.narration: People in a Bangladeshi pocket were surrounded by India, and people in an Indian pocket by Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Surrounded By The Other

scenes.narration: Some were so small that they were only a few paddy fields or a single house.
scenes.headline: Tiny Pockets Of Land

scenes.narration: Walking to the market meant leaving your country, and often your schools, roads and power with it.
scenes.headline: Cut Off From Services

scenes.narration: Many people there had little access to school or electricity, because neither government could easily reach them.
scenes.headline: No Easy Access

scenes.narration: Then there was Dahala Khagrabari, a patch of India inside Bangladesh inside India inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: That is three layers of land wrapped around one small Indian field. It was the only place like it in the world.
scenes.headline: Three Layers

scenes.narration: Everyone knew it was absurd, and for decades neither side could agree on a fix.
scenes.headline: Nobody Could Fix It

scenes.narration: Finally, in 2015, India and Bangladesh agreed to swap them. Around a hundred and sixty enclaves changed sides.
scenes.headline: The 2015 Swap

scenes.narration: At midnight on thirty-first July 2015, the pockets were handed over, and residents got to choose their country.
scenes.headline: Midnight Handover

scenes.narration: The old knot is gone, but the story shows how a line on paper can trap real people.
scenes.headline: A Knot Undone

scenes.narration: So Britain owns land in Cyprus, but India once had land inside land inside land.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: Tomorrow: more places on the map that should not exist, but do.
scenes.headline: Tomorrow
